summary: August's scan shows agent systems maturing around artifact-level evaluation, governed execution, and runtime tool security. The strongest commercial signals were Emergent's $1.5B coding-agent round, Freehand's $75M vertical-agent Series B, Suno's $5.4B financing, and Meta's acquisition of PlayAI.

trends.learn: Artifact-level evaluation; MCP/A2A tool use; multi-agent coordination; deception detection; zero-trust containment
trends.build: Vertical workers; agent evaluation; audit trails; secure sandboxes

startup_thesis.wave_1_2023_2025: Foundation models and chatbots — captured by incumbents; model access is commoditizing.
startup_thesis.wave_2_2025_now: Vertical agents plus governed infrastructure. Buyers pay for measurable workflow outcomes, security, auditability, and control planes.
startup_thesis.wave_3_2026_2028: Physical AI, multimodal world models, and specialized edge inference. Safety and containment become product requirements.
startup_thesis.where_to_play: First: governed agent operations combining permissions, budgets, memory, observability, replay, and tool security. Second: vertical agents with measurable ROI. Third: multimodal edge and physical-AI infrastructure.

market_summary: July funding validated three distinct winners: vertical operational agents (Freehand, $75M Series B), AI software production (Emergent, $1.5B valuation), and multimodal creation/embodiment (Suno at $5.4B; PlayAI acquired by Meta; X Square Robot above $2.8B).
